humanities_role_explanation: Historical newspaper text (BLN600, 19th-century British press) supplies the items, but the competence tested is generic post-OCR string correction measured by CER reduction; no disciplinary interpretive competence is assessed.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: OCR text strings are input and human re-keyed transcriptions are targets. Images are the origin of the OCR but are not given to the models.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Post-OCR correction framed as sequence-to-sequence translation (BART) or prompt-based instruction-following (Llama 2 'Fix the OCR errors in the provided text'). Error types include substitutions, insertions, deletions, misnamed entities and hallucinations.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task study on post-OCR correction using one corpus (BLN600); not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Llama 2 7B and 13B (instruction-tuned with LoRA) compared with fine-tuned BART base/large.

quantitative_metrics.note: Percentage reduction in character error rate (CER).

summary: The paper instruction-tunes Llama 2 (7B, 13B) for post-OCR correction of BLN600, a parallel corpus of 19th-century British newspaper articles, and compares it with fine-tuned BART. Llama 2 13B achieves a 54.51% CER reduction against 23.30% for BART large, and performs well with limited training data.
key_findings: Llama 2 13B reduced CER by 54.51%, Llama 2 7B by 43.26%, BART large by 23.30% and BART base by 14.60%. Llama 2 does well from the outset with small training sets, while BART improves substantially as training data grows. Substitutions and deletions are easiest to correct; insertions and heavily corrupted named entities are hardest.
facets_explanation: The ground truth consists of manually re-keyed human transcriptions from the source images, which comes with the BLN600 corpus (Booth et al., 2024) and was not created for this study. Scoring is against one reference per segment via CER. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement or alternative readings.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports a CER Reduction (%) of 54.51 for Llama 2 13B, 43.26 for Llama 2 7B, 23.30 for BART 400M and 14.60 for BART 140M; the best score is the percentage reduction in CER, not a plain accuracy. The dataset size of 13,192 is the total number of sequence pairs (train 10,400, test 2,792). No human baseline is reported, and the single English corpus means no cross-cultural comparison arises.

humanities_role.quote: Poor OCR quality continues to be a major obstacle for humanities scholars seeking to make use of digitised primary sources such as historical newspapers.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: By instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it to a fine-tuned BART on BLN600

gold_source.quote: This dataset contains OCR text sourced from British Library Newspapers along with manually re-keyed human transcriptions.
